proof.criterion: A1, the merge rule: on LINUX's replay the change is not slower - the median of three head runs uses no more whole-process CPU-seconds than the highest of three base runs. Six runs alternating, base first, in one session on one pod (m-base-1 20:04:38Z, m-head-1 20:47:39Z, m-base-2 21:30:29Z, m-head-2 22:13:08Z, m-base-3 22:55:52Z, m-head-3 23:38:15Z).
proof.surface: the Dispatch server (packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch) under the INFRA-639 replay client, LINUX's write log of 2026-10-26 22:55-23:34Z
proof.observed: Dispatch CPU-seconds base 422.01 / 415.71 / 402.50 (spread 19.51), head 404.69 / 385.15 / 393.06. The median head run 393.06 is 28.95 CPU-s below the highest base run 422.01. Not every head run is below every base run: m-head-1 404.69 is above m-base-3 402.50, two runs ninety minutes apart and well inside the base's own spread. Every run: saturated false, 174 writes sent with 0 failed, box_busy_before 0.9-1.3%, and replay.end_state.sha256 aa48884b08c5... on all six, so both builds did the same work. Every status equal (920x200, 40x201, 10x409 for the stale precondition, 2x400 for the HTML refusal) and all 522 markdown SHA-256s equal. 593 field positions differ, every one a minted block id or a token carrying one, and a base-against-base control run of the same build differs in exactly the same 593 positions (diff of the two position lists is empty), so base-against-head minus base-against-base is empty and the head introduces nothing.

trickyParts: The token reuse (N1) is exact only because a document token carries no block identity, so the stamp between the precondition check and the batch cannot change it; TestStampingBlockIDsChangesNoDocumentToken pins that.

editTree may hand back applyLive's own validated tree: that is sound because the stamp mints nothing on a tree whose ids are all there (BlockIDRepairCount is EnsureBlockIDsCount's own walk), so the tree and its validity are left as they are.

The refusals that read a write's changed blocks read them against the tree each one holds, and the accept path changes its tree twice more (padding its tables, settling what it wrote), so matchBlocks keeps only what depends on the tree the write started from and lastAfter(after) is read per tree.

pmdoc's exported function and its ValidDocument method share one core, so a test comparing the two cannot catch a wrong core; what catches one is the base-against-head write corpus and the two differential tests (BlockIndexes against BlockIndex, the text walk against the delta comparison).
deviations: The plan's measurement build (a counter of Validate calls, n_base and n_head) was not built: with the architect's rule of 2026-10-29 (S and E are evidence, not a gate) the same fact is read from the profiles, where Validate under the edit subtree falls from 0.82/0.74/0.75 s to 0.11/0.13/0.14 s.

The measured pair is main 2d3a725f against the merge head, not the plan's merge base: the branch was forward-merged twice, once to take main's docs race job and once to resolve pmdoc/find.go against #2480's QuoteFinder rewrite, so only the merge's second parent judges this change.
N1, N3 and N5 were built beyond the plan, at the architect's direction. N2, N4 and N6 are not built, each with its evidence and its head share in the pull request body.
The equivalence corpus is 23 real LINUX specs and A5's is ten, not all 1,204: each spec costs about 40 s a side and the dumps are byte-compared, so more specs buy repetition rather than coverage.

The FindQuote benchmark is the tester's throwaway, not a committed one, and it measures the preallocation alone; the validation a reused finder skips is the tester's A4 by agreement with the architect.
discoveredComplexity: Two re-pin drains replaced this pod mid-round. Nothing of a measurement survives a replacement: the load-test root, its Postgres, the restored replay seed and both prepared templates are rebuilt from nothing, about forty minutes before the first write. Evidence that must outlive a drain goes to a Dispatch artifact (infra646-round2-evidence-tgz, infra646-measurement-tgz, the tester's infra646-tester-round1-tgz).

stack.sh identifies its processes by pid and each role has its own PID namespace, so a stack another role left running is invisible to ps and blocks stack.sh start on its port. The fix is to ask that role to stop it (INFRA-639 owns the bug).
The six runs of this round and the tester's six are on different pods and are not comparable with each other; each pair is read within itself.
Round 3 is the review's: the merge with main, the cutover of the exported pmdoc forms the methods replaced, and the prose that claimed more than the code does.
